title: Duel of the day: pawn takes queen has its own hand-written fight scene - she starts casting, his shield gets there first. An animated chess game for Windows PC.
text:
Most captures in Pixel Pawns pull one of the attacker's execution routines at random, but a handful of matchups have choreography written just for them. Pawn takes queen is one of those: the queen raises her hands to cast, the soldier's shield bash arrives first, and the caption reads THE QUEEN, BY A COMMON SOLDIER. If you have ever wanted chess where the pieces fight instead of quietly vanishing, the chess duel animations cover every capture on the board. It is offline chess with no ads and no accounts - four AI strengths from Squire to Warlord, or hotseat chess with a friend on one keyboard.

https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX

title: 34 capture match-ups in this indie chess game each have their own named death scene - The Tower Is Unmade, The Mitre Rolls, Backhanded Into Oblivion
text:
Pixel Pawns is a retro pixel chess game where the board stops on a capture and the two pieces settle it themselves. 34 attacker-victim match-ups have their own name and pull the matching routine out of the attacker's own move set: the king's great cleave, the rook's two-fisted ground-pound, the queen's petrifying flick of the wrist. A few pairs get an extra hand-staged opening on top - two pawns cross blades twice before one of them finds the gap. The animated chess battles run in the same engine that draws the board, so this pixel art strategy game holds together as one piece of art; play it as two player chess on one keyboard, or against four AI levels from Squire to Warlord.

https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX
